episode.title: Synchronize native PTY exit with public lifecycle completion and make finalization resilient
episode.before: At parent 09e048fd61bc56df18676211f65703e7f0075f3a, PTY execution completed only from the public pty.onExit callback. On Windows ConPTY, native process termination could occur without that callback when the data pipe remained open, leaving the execution result unresolved and the PTY reported active. A resize requested before the first data event could also remain deferred inside the PTY implementation and throw after native process exit. In addition, exceptions from output listeners could reject the serialized processing chain or interrupt final rendering and exit notification, preventing cleanup and result completion.
episode.after: At 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324, the service observes the Windows PTY agent's native exit callback and exit-code state, schedules a 150 ms drain window, and invokes the same idempotent exit handler if the public exit event is lost. It suppresses only post-exit resize operations and the PTY library's specific already-exited resize error. Output emission, processing-chain rejection, final rendering, and exit-listener failures are contained so cleanup and result completion continue. Active PTY state is removed during finalization and activity/resize checks consult ownership and native-exit state.
episode.diff: The commit modifies packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts and its tests. It introduces a typed internal Windows-agent adapter; wraps agent resize; extracts an idempotent handlePtyExit path shared by public and native exit signals; adds a resettable 150 ms native-exit fallback; makes output and finalization callbacks exception-tolerant; treats rejected output processing as drained for finalization; removes active ownership before asynchronous log cleanup; and tightens activity and resize checks. Three regression tests cover a missing public exit event, a deferred post-exit resize, and an output-listener exception during shutdown.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 29379, with parent 09e048fd61bc56df18676211f65703e7f0075f3a and two modified files.

The parent implementation registered finalization exclusively through pty.onExit; the callback set exited, destroyed the PTY, waited for processingChain or abort, then finalized and completed the lifecycle result.
evidence_units.source: git show 09e048fd61bc56df18676211f65703e7f0075f3a:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, former onExit/finalize block around lines 1339-1451

evidence_units.claim: In the parent, output and binary events called consumers without exception containment, processingChain had no rejection recovery, final render called render(true) directly, and the exit event listener was invoked directly.
evidence_units.source: git show 09e048fd61bc56df18676211f65703e7f0075f3a:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, former renderFn, handleOutput, and finalize blocks around lines 1240-1451

evidence_units.claim: The change defines the internal Windows PTY agent fields used to detect native termination and explains that public onExit may be lost because socket closure can lag or never occur, while pre-ready resize callbacks may execute after process exit.
evidence_units.source: git diff 09e048fd61bc56df18676211f65703e7f0075f3a 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324 -- packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts; WindowsPtyAgentInternal documentation and DestroyablePty extension

evidence_units.claim: The implementation wraps the native process-exit callback in a finally block, records the native exit code, and schedules a resettable 150 ms fallback that calls the shared exit handler if public PTY exit has not arrived.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, scheduleNativeExitFallback and _$onProcessExit wrapper around lines 1541-1578

evidence_units.claim: The shared exit handler is idempotent, cancels the fallback timer, destroys the PTY, finalizes output and history, deletes active PTY ownership, and completes the lifecycle result; the normal pty.onExit callback delegates to it.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, handlePtyExit/finalize and pty.onExit delegation around lines 1371-1591

evidence_units.claim: Activity reporting now returns false when neither PTY nor child-process ownership exists, and resizePty returns without resizing when the internal agent already has an exit code.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, isPtyActive around line 1678 and resizePty around lines 1816-1827

evidence_units.claim: A regression test simulates native Windows agent exit without invoking pty.onExit, advances beyond the flush window, and asserts that the result resolves with exit code 0 and the PID is no longer active.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts, test 'should resolve execution when Windows ConPTY native _agent._$onProcessExit fires but pty.onExit is lost due to ConPTY pipe retention'

evidence_units.claim: The service replaces the agent resize function with a guard that ignores calls after native exit and suppresses only the known already-exited PTY error, rethrowing unrelated errors.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, agent.resize wrapper around lines 1118-1135

evidence_units.claim: A regression test queues resize before PTY readiness, triggers native exit, flushes the deferred resize during the first data event, and asserts that the flush does not throw.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts, test 'should prevent deferred WindowsTerminal _agent.resize from throwing synchronously during _socket data event after process exit'

evidence_units.claim: The public resizePty operation is the lifecycle boundary through which terminal-size changes reach an active PTY; the fix also guards the deeper deferred agent resize because the exception can occur after the public call returns.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, static resizePty implementation and WindowsPtyAgentInternal rationale

evidence_units.claim: Output, binary-progress, final-render, and exit-listener callbacks are wrapped with warning-and-continue handling, and processingChain gains a terminal catch so one rejected chunk does not poison subsequent shutdown processing.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.ts, renderFn, handleOutput, and handlePtyExit/finalize changes around lines 1293-1539

evidence_units.claim: A regression test makes the downstream data-event listener throw once, then emits public PTY exit and asserts that result completion wins a 500 ms race and preserves exit code 0.
evidence_units.source: git show 4577750da8e9fcee42297a2f54fbae18c0fa6324:packages/core/src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts, test 'should still finalize and resolve execution when pty.onExit fires even if an output chunk handler in processingChain rejected'

evidence_units.claim: The added test suite supplies direct behavioral oracles for all three corrected failure modes: native-exit fallback completion, safe deferred resize, and finalization after output-handler failure.

candidate_atomics.name: reconcile-native-exit-with-pty-completion
candidate_atomics.title: Reconcile native process exit with PTY lifecycle completion
candidate_atomics.description: Observe a lower-level process-exit signal, allow a bounded output-drain interval, and route a missing public exit notification through the same idempotent cleanup and result-completion path.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure a terminated subprocess cannot leave its PTY execution result pending merely because the public exit event is lost.
semantic_action.pre_state: The native process has reported an exit code, while the public PTY exit callback may still be pending or permanently absent and the execution is still marked active.
semantic_action.post_state: After a bounded drain window, exactly one shared exit path destroys the PTY, records completion, removes active ownership, and resolves the execution with the native exit code unless the public exit path completed first.
semantic_action.validation: Simulate native exit without public PTY exit, advance beyond the drain window, and assert result resolution, preserved exit code, and inactive lifecycle state.

candidate_atomics.name: guard-deferred-resize-after-process-exit
candidate_atomics.title: Neutralize deferred resize work after process exit
candidate_atomics.description: Guard the actual deferred resize target with native-exit state so a resize queued while the PTY was unready cannot crash cleanup when executed after termination.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent asynchronously deferred terminal resize work from throwing after the underlying process has exited.
semantic_action.pre_state: A resize request may have been queued before PTY readiness and can execute after native process termination, outside the original caller's synchronous error boundary.
semantic_action.post_state: Resize work becomes a no-op when native exit is known; the specific already-exited resize error is contained, while unrelated resize errors remain observable.
semantic_action.validation: Queue a resize before readiness, mark the native process exited, flush the deferred callback, and assert that it does not throw.

candidate_atomics.name: isolate-output-failures-from-finalization
candidate_atomics.title: Keep output failures from blocking process finalization
candidate_atomics.description: Contain consumer and rendering exceptions at output boundaries and make shutdown wait tolerate an already-rejected processing chain so cleanup and lifecycle completion still run.

semantic_action.intent: Guarantee process cleanup and result resolution even when downstream output handling fails.
semantic_action.pre_state: A data, binary-progress, final-render, or exit-event consumer can throw, or an earlier output task can reject while process exit is being finalized.
semantic_action.post_state: Output failures are logged and contained; the shutdown barrier settles, final cleanup executes, and the process result resolves with its exit information.
semantic_action.validation: Make a data-event consumer throw, emit process exit, and assert that execution resolves before a timeout with the expected exit code.

candidate_workflows.name: harden-pty-exit-and-finalization-lifecycle
candidate_workflows.title: Make PTY termination deterministic across asynchronous exit and output paths
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for PTY integrations where native process exit, public exit delivery, deferred control operations, and output callbacks can become desynchronized.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure that a natively terminated PTY process reaches exactly one completed lifecycle state after bounded output draining, without deferred resize or output-consumer failures preventing cleanup.
when_to_use: A PTY-backed subprocess can terminate at the operating-system layer without reliably producing the library's public exit event.
Control operations may be queued internally and execute after process termination.
Output or lifecycle event consumers are outside the lifecycle owner's trust boundary and may throw during output processing or shutdown.
anti_goals: Do not immediately finalize at the native exit signal when a short bounded window is needed to drain trailing PTY output.

Do not suppress arbitrary resize, rendering, or consumer errors indiscriminately; contain only errors whose failure must not block lifecycle completion, and preserve logging or rethrow unrelated control errors.
Do not create separate cleanup implementations for native and public exit signals.
Do not change command semantics, output formatting, or successful interactive behavior beyond lifecycle hardening.
not_applicable_when: The subprocess API provides one authoritative exit signal that is guaranteed to fire only after output has drained and no lower-level termination signal is available or needed.
No PTY, deferred control-operation queue, or asynchronous output-finalization pipeline is involved.
The desired behavior is to keep a process logically active after confirmed native termination.
inputs: PTY process handle and public exit subscription
native process-exit signal or queryable exit state
PTY control operations that may be deferred
workflow_graph.entry_state: A PTY execution is registered as active; output and control callbacks may still be pending; public exit delivery is not sufficient to prove timely native termination completion.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Native or public exit has selected one idempotent finalization path; trailing output received during the bounded window has been processed as far as possible; listener failures cannot block cleanup; PTY ownership is removed; and the execution result is resolved with exit metadata.

steps.condition: The PTY implementation can defer resize or another control operation beyond the initiating call.
steps.validation: A control operation queued before readiness executes after native exit without throwing, while unrelated errors are not silently swallowed.

steps.condition: Output, rendering, or exit consumers can throw or reject independently of process state.
steps.validation: An injected output-consumer exception does not prevent the public exit path from resolving the execution result.

steps.condition: A native exit signal or already-populated native exit code is observable before reliable public exit completion.
steps.validation: With the public exit event withheld, native exit resolves the result after the drain window, records the exit code, and clears active state.

validation_ladder: Unit-test the post-exit control-operation guard by flushing a previously deferred resize after native termination.
Unit-test ordinary public-exit finalization with a throwing output consumer and a bounded completion timeout.
Unit-test the missing-public-exit scenario using the native exit signal, the complete drain interval, result metadata, and active-resource state.
Confirm both native and public exit signals converge on one idempotent finalizer so duplicate completion and cleanup are prevented.
stop_conditions: Stop if there is no trustworthy native termination signal or exit state to reconcile with the public lifecycle.
Stop if no bounded drain policy can be justified; an unbounded wait recreates the hang, while immediate cleanup may discard output.
Stop if the proposed interception requires swallowing unrelated operational errors or bypassing the normal shared cleanup path.
Stop and defer promotion if the regression tests cannot establish result resolution and resource-state cleanup.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle does not include PR discussion, review rationale, or CI/status-check results.

The regression tests are present as direct validation oracles, but this extraction did not establish an independent local test-run result because the supplied working tree has its tracked files removed; evidence was inspected from the pinned Git objects.
The 150 ms drain duration is repository-specific evidence and should remain a configurable parameter rather than a universal constant.

unresolved_questions: Were the three regression tests executed successfully in CI for PR 29379? Status-check metadata is unavailable in the supplied evidence bundle.
What measurements or PTY-library guarantees motivated the specific 150 ms drain interval? The implementation and tests establish the value used, but not a cross-project timing rule.
The commit comment and test describe a Windows ConPTY-specific lost-exit mechanism; applicability to other PTY implementations requires independent evidence.
